docs.title: About
docs.text: Steve Nesbitt is a Professor and Department Head in the Department of Climate, Meteorology & Atmospheric Sciences (CliMAS) at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he has been a faculty member since 2006. His research focuses on radar and satellite meteorology, mesoscale convective systems, tropical and subtropical meteorology, cloud microphysics, and data science applied to the water cycle and high-impact weather. He is recognized for leading major international field campaigns studying cloud dynamics and physics and high-impact weather.

docs.title: Research Focus Areas
docs.text:
• Global Precipitation Science — Satellite and ground-based remote sensing of precipitation across the tropics and subtropics.
  • Convective Storms & Severe Weather — Dynamics and structure of organized convective systems and their role in severe weather.
  • Radar & Remote Sensing — Polarimetric radar theory, retrieval algorithms, and open-source radar software.
  • Terrain–Precipitation Coupling — Orographic effects on convection and precipitation in complex terrain environments.
  • Cloud Microphysics & Snowfall — Particle size distributions, lake-effect snow, and radar microphysical retrievals.
  • Urban Hydrometeorology — Urban effects on precipitation and flooding.

docs.title: Textbook
docs.text:
Radar Meteorology: A First Course Robert M. Rauber and Stephen W. Nesbitt Wiley-Blackwell, 2018 · 488 pp.

Radar Meteorology: A First Course is a graduate-level textbook designed for students encountering weather radar for the first time. It covers the physical principles of radar, signal processing, polarimetric observables, precipitation estimation, severe weather applications, and emerging radar technologies. The book is used in ATMS 410 (Radar Meteorology) at the University of Illinois and at universities worldwide.

docs.title: Field Campaigns
docs.text: Steve Nesbitt has participated in 27 major field campaigns spanning 1998–2025, spanning roles from radiosonde scientist and aircraft scientist to principal investigator of large multi-agency international deployments.

docs.title: RELAMPAGO-CACTI (2018–2019)
docs.text:
Remote sensing of Electrification, Lightning, And Mesoscale/microscale Processes with Adaptive Ground Observations — Cloud, Aerosol, and Complex Terrain Interactions Córdoba, Argentina

Lead Principal Investigator of a $25M+ joint NSF/DOE/NASA/NOAA initiative deploying over 100 scientists across 7 agencies in Argentina. RELAMPAGO-CACTI studied extreme convective storms, orographic convection, and cloud microphysics in the lee of the Andes.

docs.title: CROCUS — Urban Climate Initiatives (2024–2025)
docs.text:
Community Research on Climate and Urban Science Chicago, IL

Principal Investigator. DOE-funded study of urban effects on precipitation, flooding, and the local water cycle in the greater Chicago metropolitan area.

docs.title: Lake Effect Snow Microphysics (2022–2024)
docs.text:
Buffalo, NY

Study of microphysical processes in lake-effect snowstorms using polarimetric radar and in situ aircraft observations.

docs.title: PERiLS (2022–2023)
docs.text:
Propagation, Evolution, and Rotation in Linear Storms Southeastern United States

Collaborative NSF/NOAA field campaign examining the mechanisms of tornado production and severe weather in quasi-linear convective systems.

docs.title: OLYMPEX (2015)
docs.text:
Olympic Mountain Experiment Pacific Northwest, USA

NASA Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) ground validation campaign examining orographic precipitation in the Olympic Mountains.

docs.title: GCPEX (2011–2012)
docs.text:
Global Precipitation Measurement Cold-season Precipitation Experiment Ontario, Canada

NASA GPM ground validation of snowfall retrieval algorithms.

docs.title: CAMP²Ex (2019)
docs.text:
Cloud, Aerosol and Monsoon Processes Philippines Experiment Philippines

NASA field campaign studying aerosol-cloud-precipitation interactions in the maritime tropical environment.

docs.title: NSF OPEL-WG (2008–2011)
docs.text:
Orographic Precipitation and Extremes over the Western Ghats Karnataka, India

Principal Investigator. Study of extreme monsoon rainfall along the windward slopes of the Western Ghats.

docs.title: Open Source Software
docs.text: The following are selected open source software projects developed or co-developed by Steve Nesbitt and his research group. All projects are hosted on GitHub.

docs.title: Py-ART
docs.text: Python ARM Radar Toolkit — A data model driven interactive toolkit for working with weather radar data. Supports reading, processing, visualizing, and writing radar data in a wide variety of formats.

docs.title: xradar
docs.text: High-speed Rust port of xradar — A tool for working with weather radar data in xarray, rewritten with Rust-backed I/O for major performance improvements in radar data ingestion and processing.

docs.title: AWOT
docs.text: Airborne Weather Observations Toolkit — A Python package for reading, analyzing, and visualizing airborne meteorological and radar data from field campaigns.

docs.title: PyDDA
docs.text: Pythonic Direct Data Assimilation — A multiple-Doppler wind retrieval package based on the 3D variational technique. Retrieves 3D wind fields from multiple Doppler radar volumes.

docs.title: CSU_RadarTools
docs.text: A module of independent functions for doing precipitation retrievals from polarimetric radar data, including hydrometeor classification, rainfall estimation, and retrievals of ice water content.

docs.title: artview
docs.text: ARM Radar Toolkit Viewer — An interactive visualization tool for weather radar data built on top of Py-ART.

docs.title: DRpy
docs.text: A Python package to open GPM Dual-frequency Precipitation Radar (DPR) files into xarray, enabling use of the full xarray ecosystem for GPM-DPR analysis.

docs.title: radar-data-polygon-viz
docs.text: Demonstration of visualization of weather radar data in its native gate/polygon structure, enabling more accurate spatial representations.

docs.title: open-radar-data
docs.text: A community repository for sharing radar datasets used across open radar software packages for testing and examples.

docs.title: rustmatrix
docs.text: A Rust-backed T-matrix scattering library for nonspherical particles, ported from pytmatrix with major performance improvements via Rust bindings.

docs.title: Snow-Scattering
docs.text: Simulations of radar backscatter in snowfall, exploring sensitivities to different axial ratios, shapes, densities, and habits.

docs.title: myPSD
docs.text: An interactive polarimetric radar particle size distribution (PSD) explorer built with rustmatrix + FastAPI + React.

docs.title: wrf-realtime
docs.text: Code to initialize and run WPS and WRF for realtime RELAMPAGO-Argentina forecasts during the 2018–2019 field campaign.

docs.title: mesomodel
docs.text: A collection of code related to mesoscale atmospheric simulation with WRF and CM1.

docs.title: LOFS-read
docs.text: Code to read, convert, and visualize Leigh Orf's CM1 I/O format (LOFS) for large-eddy simulation output.

docs.title: ARradar
docs.text: Python tools to read and analyze data from Argentine weather radars, developed in support of the RELAMPAGO field campaign.

docs.title: ams-2020-ml-python-course
docs.text: Machine Learning in Python for Environmental Science Problems — Materials for the AMS 2020 Short Course.

docs.title: uiuc-atmos-computing
docs.text: Documentation and tutorials for scientific computing within the Department of Climate, Meteorology & Atmospheric Sciences at the University of Illinois.

docs.title: era5-mcp-server
docs.text: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for accessing ERA5 reanalysis data.

docs.title: ipynbhpc
docs.text: Utilities for running Jupyter notebooks interactively on HPC (high-performance computing) systems.

docs.text:

He currently serves as Chief Editor, Atmosphere section, Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology.

docs.title: RELAMPAGO–Argentina WRF Forecasts
docs.text: During the RELAMPAGO-CACTI field campaign (2018–2019), the Nesbitt group operated a real-time Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model system providing daily convective-scale forecasts over the Córdoba province of Argentina.

docs.title: About the Forecasts
docs.text:
The real-time WRF forecasting system was developed and run by Steve Nesbitt's group at the University of Illinois to support operational decision-making during RELAMPAGO field operations. Forecasts were used by scientists and flight crews to identify optimal sampling targets for ground-based and airborne instruments.

  • Model: WRF-ARW (Weather Research and Forecasting – Advanced Research WRF)
  • Domain: Córdoba Province, Argentina and surroundings
  • Focus: Convective initiation and evolution in the lee of the Andes

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
The initialization and run scripts used for the real-time WRF system are available on GitHub:

wrf-realtime — Code to initialize and run WPS and WRF for real-time RELAMPAGO forecasts.

docs.title: About RELAMPAGO-CACTI
docs.text:
RELAMPAGO (Remote sensing of Electrification, Lightning, And Mesoscale/microscale Processes with Adaptive Ground Observations) was a joint NSF, DOE, NASA, and NOAA field campaign conducted in Córdoba, Argentina in November–December 2018, with a follow-on campaign in early 2019.

As Lead Principal Investigator, Steve Nesbitt coordinated 100+ scientists from 7 agencies across the United States and Argentina to study:

  • Extreme convective storms in the lee of the Andes
  • Orographic forcing of deep convection
  • Cloud microphysics and precipitation processes
  • Lightning and electrification in subtropical storms

Total budget: $25M+ across all partner agencies.
